collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ROLE MODELS AND GOOD EXAMPLES, RM-41 to RM-90 (draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Fifty more events continuing your "Role Models and Good Examples — 40 Events". Same shape as yours: a SETUP, choices A-D (a few have three), and two possible outcomes per choice; the game picks one outcome from the chosen choice.

ledger.before: A villager who always covers the communal water jar to keep insects out notices
ledger.after: (Name1), who always covers the communal water jar to keep insects out, notices
ledger.why: the owner (2026-11-15): the person the event is about is a cast villager shown by name, the role word kept as flavor (the villager need not have that job)

collection.description: A villager who always covers the communal water jar notices a small child doing the same without being asked.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (Name1), who always covers the communal water jar to keep insects out, notices a small child doing the same thing without being asked.

choices.label: Teach the Child Why It Matters.
Ask the Child to Help Remind Others.

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: The child beams and covers every jar in sight.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: The child shrugs and says, "You always do it," and runs off to play.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: The villager feels a quiet pride that the habit has spread.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: The villager wonders how many other habits the child has picked up, and resolves to be careful.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: The child asks a dozen questions about insects and water.

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: The child already knew why, and explains it back proudly.

d1.name: Outcome D1
d1.text: The child becomes the village's cheerful jar guardian.

d2.name: Outcome D2
d2.text: The child takes the job a little too seriously, and everyone smiles at the stern reminders.
